input.summary: Meridian has 251 AI use cases catalogued; only 26 are active — all blocked by absent data foundations.
covers: Governed data foundation for AI / LLM automation
sources: Contact center transcript and telephony platform

story.meaning: Meridian has catalogued a credible AI use-case portfolio spanning clinical, financial, and operational domains — but zero use cases can advance to production without resolving five compounding foundation gaps.
story.observed: 251 use cases identified; 26 active, 225 candidate. No certified medallion architecture, no patient/member identity spine, no formal data governance, no AI audit trail, and no governed semantic layer are evidenced across any domain.
story.matters: Every high-priority use case — lakehouse, prior-auth automation, call center AI, cost transparency, payment integrity — shares the same upstream blockers. Delay on foundations compounds across all seven workstreams simultaneously.
story.supports: Decision gate: fund and sequence foundation work first — medallion architecture, identity spine, governance operating model, and audit trail — before committing AI deployment budgets to any individual use case.

findings: 225 of 251 use cases remain in candidate status; the 10% active rate signals a portfolio that is aspirationally large but foundationally unready to execute.

All five top-priority use cases share the same three blockers: no certified medallion architecture, no patient/member identity spine, and no formal data governance operating model — meaning a single foundation investment unlocks the entire portfolio.

SAS analytics estate is the current detection engine for payment integrity, but model lineage is ungoverned; this creates regulatory and recovery-quantification risk that grows with every new AI use case layered on top.

No AI audit trail evidence exists across any use case — a material model-risk and compliance exposure that must be resolved before any LLM or automated decisioning use case can be approved for production.

chain: AI use cases → require → Governed data foundation (semantic layer + audit trail)
Governed data foundation → requires → Medallion architecture (AWS/Databricks — target direction)
Medallion architecture → requires → Patient/member identity spine
Identity spine → requires → EMR + Claims + Pharmacy harmonization (Epic Clarity, Claims platform, Pharmacy platform)
Call center AI → requires → Transcript governance + real-time CRM integration + intent taxonomy
Payment integrity AI → requires → SAS model lineage governance + provider entity resolution + recovery workflow evidence
Provider quality AI → requires → HEDIS/STAR logic certification + attribution ownership + contract linkage
relationships.note: All seven priority use cases share a common dependency chain rooted in the same five foundation gaps; resolving the foundation layer is a force-multiplier — it unblocks the entire portfolio rather than a single workstream.

gaps.missing: No certified medallion architecture on AWS/Databricks
gaps.blocks: Unified clinical + claims lakehouse; all downstream AI/LLM use cases
gaps.needed: Certified bronze/silver/gold layer with Epic Clarity, Claims, and Pharmacy data loaded and reconciled
gaps.handoff: CDAO + CIO to own architecture certification gate; CFO to validate cost model before build commitment

gaps.blocks: Lakehouse longitudinal view; call center member identity linkage; provider attribution
gaps.needed: Governed identity resolution across EMR, claims, pharmacy, and CRM member records
gaps.handoff: Chief Data Officer to assign identity spine ownership; Health Plan Ops and Clinical Ops to co-sign member matching rules

gaps.missing: No formal data governance operating model
gaps.blocks: All AI/LLM automation use cases; semantic layer certification; data quality rule enforcement
gaps.needed: Governance charter, data steward assignments, policy enforcement, and operating cadence
gaps.handoff: CDAO to stand up governance council; Legal and Compliance to ratify AI policy framework

gaps.missing: No AI audit trail evidence across any use case
gaps.blocks: All LLM and automated decisioning use cases; model risk sign-off; regulatory defensibility
gaps.needed: Human-in-the-loop controls, model decision logging, and lineage documentation per use case
gaps.handoff: Chief Risk Officer and Compliance to define audit trail standard; CDAO to enforce as activation gate

gaps.missing: SAS model lineage ungoverned; provider entity resolution unproven
gaps.blocks: Payment integrity leakage quantification; FWA detection defensibility; recovery realization tracking
gaps.needed: Governed lineage for all SAS detection models; certified provider entity graph; investigation and recovery workflow evidence
gaps.handoff: Health Plan Ops and Finance to co-own recovery baseline; Analytics to document SAS model lineage before any migration or augmentation

evidence.name: AI & Automation Use Cases Dataset
evidence.facts: 183 high-confidence and 68 medium-confidence evidence items across 246 evidence references. All active use cases carry at least one unresolved foundation gap.
evidence.fields: use_case, data_domain, systems, value_hypothesis, evidence_needed, confidence, active_candidate_status
evidence.supports: Portfolio scope, confidence distribution, and gap mapping across all seven priority use cases
evidence.missing: No certified production baselines; no realized-value actuals; AWS/Databricks foundation not yet evidenced

evidence.name: Unified Clinical + Claims Lakehouse Evidence Bundle
evidence.facts: Epic Clarity, Caboodle, Claims platform, and Pharmacy platform identified as source systems. No certified medallion architecture, no identity spine, and no claims/pharmacy harmonization evidenced.
evidence.supports: Foundation gap identification for the highest-priority strategic use case
evidence.missing: Medallion architecture certification; identity spine load confirmation; AWS/Databricks readiness evidence

evidence.name: Governed Data Foundation / AI-LLM Automation Evidence Bundle
evidence.rows: 3 active items (prior authorization, coding, utilization management)
evidence.facts: No formal data governance operating model, no certified semantic layer, no AI audit trail, and no data quality rules evidenced. Blocks all LLM and automated decisioning use cases.
evidence.supports: Governance and audit trail gap identification blocking all AI/LLM activation gates
evidence.missing: Governance charter; semantic layer certification; AI audit trail standard; data quality rule registry

evidence.name: Payment Integrity and Leakage Reduction Evidence Bundle
evidence.rows: 3 active items (claims anomalies, FWA, billing patterns)
evidence.facts: SAS analytics estate is current detection platform. Model lineage ungoverned. Provider entity resolution unproven. Investigation and recovery workflows not evidenced.
evidence.supports: Payment integrity risk exposure and leakage quantification gap
evidence.missing: SAS model lineage documentation; provider entity graph certification; recovery realization tracking

evidence.name: Call Center Optimization Evidence Bundle
evidence.rows: 3 active items (transcripts, CRM cases, claims status)
evidence.facts: Genesys, Salesforce Health Cloud, and Claims platform identified. Transcript governance, real-time integration, intent taxonomy, and member identity linkage all unproven.
evidence.supports: Contact center AI readiness gap; AHT/FCR baseline absence
evidence.missing: Transcript governance policy; real-time CRM integration proof; intent taxonomy certification; AHT and FCR baselines
